title: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation
creator: Marcus Li
description: Implement a lightweight, portable function-schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The mapper will normalize model-declared function schemas into SDK-native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful-degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry/backoff for non-streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume/fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (py/ts/go) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and JSON validators
Invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including: call(), stream_call(), call_with_idempotency(), and fallback_to_text()
Retry/backoff policy supports at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers
Streaming handshake protocol enables resume from KV-prefix if server supports resume tokens; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server-side best-effort completion
Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover schema coercion, optional argument handling, enum coercion, nested objects, and streaming resume scenarios
Documentation pages and three example apps (py/ts/go) demonstrating function call patterns and recommended safety knobs
design_notes: Keep mapper small: generate validator code at package build-time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models
Prefer permissive coercion by default (string->enum, numeric strings->numbers) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation

Streaming handshake: introduce a small four-step exchange (CLIENT_HELLO -> SERVER_ACK(with resume_token?) -> CLIENT_STREAM_START -> KEEPALIVE frames). If SERVER_ACK includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non-side-effecting tools
Idempotency token strategy: allow user-provided token or generate RFC4122 v4 by default; include an optional idempotency window header so routers can garbage-collect tokens early
Telemetry: emit events for schema_mismatch, coercion_event, retry_attempt, retry_abort_reason, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure
Trade-offs: full schema strictness reduces user errors but increases friction for rapid prototyping. Default to permissive but log and surface mismatches via console warnings and SDK diagnostics API
implementation_plan: Week 1: Implement core schema mapper library in a neutral TypeScript reference package with a minimal runtime validator interface
Week 2: Port mapper to Python and Go wrappers, add generator to produce thin language bindings (type stubs for py, d.ts for ts, go structs)
Week 3: Implement streaming handshake protocol and client-side resume logic; add resume_token plumbing to server contract (spec PR)
Week 4: Add invocation helpers with retry policies and idempotency token handling; expose policy knobs via client config
Week 5: Tests, examples, docs, and API reviews. Prepare SDK release artifacts and coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for telemetry keys and server-side resume support
test_plan: Unit: validator coercion matrix for primitives, enums, nested objects and arrays
Integration: end-to-end example calling a toy function (echo, counter) in all three SDKs verifying idempotency behavior
Chaos: simulate dropped connections during streaming and assert resume/fallback semantics and no double-execution where exact-once is requested
Performance: measure additional latency/cpu of runtime validation under high QPS and validate generator reduces runtime overhead
Security: fuzz malformed schemas and inputs to ensure validators fail closed when strict mode is enabled
rollout_plan: Alpha: release TypeScript reference package and experimental Python wrapper to internal SDK alpha channel; invite 3 beta customers to opt-in
Beta: widen to public SDK releases behind feature flag (enable_schema_mapper=true) and collect telemetry for coercion events
GA: enable by default with documentation and migration guide. Coordinate with runtime team to stop accepting legacy unstructured tool formats once 90% of clients migrated or after 3 months
Backward compatibility: provide an adapter that maps old 'tools' flat payload to new function schema descriptors for 6 months
